Investing in a new comfortable, durable bike saddle is a great way to upgrade your bicycle and improve your overall cycling experience. Bike saddles come in different lengths, widths, shapes, and rails and there are saddles with memory foam, gel, and some with no padding at all. 

On mountain trails you will probably be in a variety of riding positions. The saddle needs to have sufficient padding for your sit bones, a durable cover, round edges, and a short nose that will allow you to move freely. You also might enjoy a central cutout that reduces pressure on the perineum area. The cut out also improves airflow which reduces moisture and friction. Everything from the padding to the width of the saddle itself is variable. Performance saddles are narrow and long allowing you to have the maximum level of power transfer while you are peddling and the least amount of thigh chafing.

There are three important elements to consider in mountain bike saddles. First, it needs some padding where your sit bones are. The padding can be made from either gel or memory foam. Although gel is cheaper and softer it gets compressed over time. Foam last longer so it's a better long term investment. Second, is a cover that requires little maintenance, should withstand the weather and be slippery enough to assuage chaffing but durable enough to withstand scratches. Third, is the rails. Saddle rails can be made from steel, titanium, or alloy. These materials affect the price and the weight.

Upgrading your bike pedals is a matter of personal preference. There are two main types, flat and clipless pedals.

Flat bike pedals have a series of studs or pins in different positions across both surfaces of the pedal. Pins are adjustable and are placed to optimize your shoe placement. Some pins or studs can be sharp and might pose a hazard. A flat pedal can also fold up, making it convenient for storage and traveling by bus and train. The wide platform of the flat peddle allows you to exert leverage during cornering and pumping hard while adjusting foot placement to gain control over the bike for different terrains. Flat pedals also have either a concave or convex rim shape. The convex shape allows easier slip and adjusting, while the concave shape boosts mud shedding properties.

Clipless pedals are a popular choice for a casual rider for a smoother ride and are great at giving you more power on each stroke.

You should look for a strong pedal with good grip because of the rough terrain and wet weather you will encounter. Pedals are made from  either a nylon composite, that can handle a lot of bashing on rocks before it sees serious wear, or a machined aluminum alloy, steel, or titanium.
